1.explanation: The ReplaceConnectionBehavior handlers (fixConnection and replaceReconnectedConnection) explicitly pass the raw Diagram-JS waypoint objects into modeling.connect, which ends up writing these JS objects to the BPMN businessObject. Since BpmnUpdater.updateConnection and updateConnectionWaypoints are empty stubs, the BPMN-DI isn’t corrected (cropped or transformed) before serialization. As a result the raw waypoint array is dropped straight into the sequenceFlow’s XML. To fix this, either strip out or transform the Diagram-JS waypoint objects in ReplaceConnectionBehavior (or in Modeling) and/or implement updateConnection/updateConnectionWaypoints in BpmnUpdater so that only proper BPMN-DI waypoint entries are produced.
1.bug_scenario: In the animated scenario the user drags a task off an existing task to automatically re-connect the two with an orthogonal connector. As soon as the connector needs a “bend” in the middle (i.e. a segment with two waypoints), the XML export ends up with an illegal waypoints property on the sequenceFlow element — literally “[object Object],[object Object],…”. This shows up as serialized marker text instead of proper BPMN-DI waypoint entries.

2.explanation:
1. ReplaceConnectionBehavior (fixConnection & replaceReconnectedConnection): when a connection is replaced or reconnected, these handlers call `modeling.connect(..., { type, waypoints: connection.waypoints.slice() })`, passing the UI waypoint array into the new business object.  
2. Modeling.prototype.connect: this API forwards the passed-in `attrs` (including `waypoints`) into the semantic element creation (`createConnection`), causing the BPMN element to gain a `waypoints` property.  
3. BpmnUpdater.prototype.updateConnectionWaypoints: the updater should move routing points into the DI section and strip them from the semantic model, but this method is empty. As a result, no cleanup happens and the illegal `waypoints` attribute remains on the `<sequenceFlow>`.  

To fix the bug, waypoints must not be persisted on the BPMN semantic element. Instead, replaceConnection handlers should stop passing waypoints into `attrs`, or BpmnUpdater.updateConnectionWaypoints must properly extract and serialize waypoints into the DI and remove them from the business object.
2.bug_scenario:
After duplicating a task with a bent arrow (a sequenceFlow that has a middle segment), the exported BPMN XML contains an illegal `waypoints` attribute on the `<sequenceFlow>` element. Instead of storing routing information only in the DI (Diagram Interchange) section, the UI waypoints are carried over into the semantic BPMN element, resulting in:  

  <sequenceFlow id="..." sourceRef="..." targetRef="..." waypoints="[object Object],[object Object],…" />
